name: Adriano Santos
action: Adriano sets the half-tensioned tom down on a folded cloth, making sure the skin doesn't shift. He wipes his hands with a rag, then with a cleaner, drying them thoroughly before moving to the tarp. He pulls the tarp back from the Ludwig kit, revealing the bass drum, toms, and snare. He says, in a flat and slightly loud voice, "Ten minutes. It's all here—toms, snare, bass, original hardware, but the snare's throw-off is sticky. I noted that in the listing. Bearing edges are clean on all of them. You can inspect it, take your time, but if you want measurements, they're in the post. Look close now, because I don't do returns over scratches that were already listed." He steps back, arms folded, standing nearby but not hovering, waiting.
reason: Adriano recognized the buyer from the listing photo and noted his hurry and mention of a studio rehearsal. He knew the tom was not at a safe point to leave—the head was half-tensioned and the glue still tacky—and he also perceived the buyer as someone likely to rush through an inspection and leave if it didn't match his imagined version. Yet he recalled buyers who never came back after being told to wait. Because the Ludwig kit had been sitting under the tarp for two days, he decided not to scare off a serious buyer over a lug he could fix in five minutes. He carefully set the tom down and cleaned his hands thoroughly before touching the shell, as he refused to handle a drum with dirty hands even for a stranger. He wanted the buyer to inspect now rather than later, to avoid a future return over a scratch already described in the listing. He invited the close inspection, specified the snare's sticky throw-off and clean bearing edges, and stepped back to let the buyer decide, accepting that if the buyer declined, his time would not be wasted.
